questions.question_text:
A courier travels $54\text{ km}$ in $45\text{ minutes}$ at constant speed.
What is the courier's speed in $\text{km/h}$?

options.why: Divides by $45$ minutes and labels the result in kilometres per hour, calculating $54 \div 45 = 1.2$.
Treats $45\text{ minutes}$ as $0.45\text{ h}$ and calculates $54 \div 0.45 = 120\text{ km/h}$.
Treats the journey time as $1\text{ h}$ and calculates $54 \div 1 = 54\text{ km/h}$.

questions.question_text:
A swimmer travels $125\text{ m}$ in $90\text{ s}$ at constant speed.
What is the swimmer's speed in $\text{m/s}$, rounded to $2$ decimal places?

options.why: Divides time by distance instead of distance by time, calculating $90 \div 125 = 0.72$.
Uses $60\text{ s}$ instead of $90\text{ s}$, calculating $125 \div 60 \approx 2.08\text{ m/s}$.
Converts $90\text{ s}$ to $1.5\text{ minutes}$, then labels $125 \div 1.5 \approx 83.33$ as metres per second.

questions.question_text:
A boat travels $4.725\text{ km}$ in $3\text{ min }30\text{ s}$ at constant speed.
What is the boat's speed in $\text{m/s}$?

options.why: Ignores the extra $30\text{ s}$ and calculates $4725 \div 180 = 26.25\text{ m/s}$.
Does not convert kilometres to metres and labels $4.725 \div 210 = 0.0225$ as metres per second.
Uses $3.5$ minutes as though it were seconds and calculates $4725 \div 3.5 = 1350\text{ m/s}$.
